title: Check the form
concept: re · checking a shape, and its limits
description: Check usernames and times on the sign-up form: the right shape first, then values that make sense.

tasks.title: Check the shape, not the truth
tasks.body: re.fullmatch() checks that a whole reply has the right shape: r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}" for a date like 2026-03-01. But the right shape is not the same as a real value: 2026-13-45 has the shape, and is no date at all.
tasks.detail:
So check the shape with a pattern, then check the meaning with code: turn the parts into numbers and test their ranges, or let a library such as datetime decide.

Real email addresses are too varied for a short pattern. One @ with text on both sides is a fair first check, and the only real test is sending a message.

tasks.note: 2026-13-45 has the right shape, so the pattern lets it through, but date() refuses month 13. 26-3-1 does not even have the shape.

tasks.question: Does re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", "2026-02-30") match?
tasks.why: A pattern only sees digits and dashes. Knowing February has no 30th takes code that understands dates.

tasks.prompt: Predict, then run: add "2028-02-29" and "2026-02-29" to the list. Then make is_date() also refuse dates before the year 2000.

Write two functions that check text.

1. valid_username(name) returns True when the name is 3 to 12 characters long, starts with a letter, and holds only letters, digits and underscores, and False otherwise.
2. valid_time(text) returns True for a 24-hour time written as two digits, a colon and two digits, with hours from 00 to 23 and minutes from 00 to 59, and False otherwise.

Do not ask for input: the check calls your functions.
tasks.starter: # Import re, then define valid_username(name) and valid_time(text)
hints: For a username, [A-Za-z] is one letter and \w is a letter, digit or underscore. {2,11} means from 2 to 11 of what comes before it.
For a time, fullmatch() with two groups checks the shape. Then turn each group into a number and check its range, and return the answer as True or False.
With other names: re.fullmatch(r"[A-Z]{2}\d{2}", plate) checks a shape, and m.group(1) can then be turned into a number with int().

error_hints.text: re is a name only after import re at the top.
fullmatch() gives None when the shape is wrong, and None has no group(). Return False before using it.
nova_7 is 6 characters, starts with a letter, and holds only letters, a digit and an underscore: True.
A name must start with a letter, so 7nova is refused.
23:59 is the last minute of the day: True.
24:00 has the right shape, but there is no hour 24: check the hours are from 00 to 23.
Check a name that is too short: at least 3 characters.
Check a name that is too long: at most 12 characters.
Check a time with a one-digit hour: the hour must be two digits.
Check the minutes: they go from 00 to 59.

similar_example.code:
import re

def valid_plate(plate):
    m = re.fullmatch(r"([A-Z]{2})(\d{2})", plate)
    if not m:
        return False
    return int(m.group(2)) >= 10

print(valid_plate("AB12"), valid_plate("AB07"), valid_plate("ab12"))
similar_example.note: A shape check, then a value check on a group. Your form has two fields with different rules.

other_ways.note: The ranges can live in the pattern itself: [01]\d or 2[0-3] for the hours, [0-5]\d for the minutes. isascii() keeps out letters such as é, which \w also accepts.
The same checks without re, letter by letter. Longer, but some people find it easier to read.

cases.description: a name that is too short
a name that is too long
a time with a one-digit hour
a time with too many minutes
